steps.title: Breed mice under SPF conditions
steps.instruction: House 2–4 C57BL/6J female mice per cage in a specific‑pathogen‑free facility at 23 ± 1 °C with a 12 h light/dark cycle (lights on 08:00, off 20:00) and provide ad libitum food and water.

steps.title: Prepare glass pipettes for oocyte handling
steps.instruction: Fabricate and sterilize glass pipettes with an inner diameter of ~150–200 µm for oocyte manipulation.

substeps.instruction: Cut each glass pipette in the middle using an ampoule glass cutter.
Heat the cut edge with an alcohol‑lamp flame to smooth it.
Hold both sides of the pipette with one hand and curved‑tip tweezers.
Re‑heat the middle until slightly softened, remove from flame, and pull both ends horizontally to create a tapered shape.
Trim excess glass, re‑heat, and gently smooth the tip; a smooth tip reduces oocyte damage.
Inspect the tip under a stereomicroscope; select pipettes with an inner diameter of ~150–200 µm.
Wrap each pipette in aluminum foil, dry‑heat sterilize at 180 °C for 30 min, and store in a new 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Prepare TYH and M2 medium dishes
steps.instruction: Set up culture dishes with TYH medium drops covered by liquid paraffin and fresh M2 medium drops for oocyte washing.

substeps.instruction: Place 100 µL TYH medium drops (one drop per spot) into 60 mm dishes and overlay each drop with liquid paraffin.
Incubate the dishes in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for at least 60 min before oocyte collection.
Thaw M2 medium, dispense four 100 µL drops into a new 60 mm dish; do not cover with paraffin or pre‑incubate.

steps.title: Collect immature oocytes from juvenile mice
steps.instruction: Isolate ovaries from 12‑, 15‑, and 21‑day‑old mice, dissociate tissue, and purify oocytes.

substeps.instruction: Wear gloves and other protective equipment; have scissors and tweezers ready.
Euthanize female mice at the specified ages by CO₂ exposure.
Disinfect the abdomen with 70 % ethanol, then make a midline incision from abdomen to chest with large scissors.
Pull the skin laterally to expose the peritoneum; cut the peritoneum with small scissors.
Shift gut and internal organs to locate the V‑shaped uterus, oviducts, and ovaries.
Grasp the utero‑tubal junction with precision tweezers and separate each ovary from the oviduct and uterus.
Trim away adipose tissue from each ovary and transfer the cleaned ovary to the TYH‑paraffin dish prepared in step C.
Using a 22‑G needle, mince each ovary into fragments in 100 µL M2 medium (see Fig. 3A).
Centrifuge the suspension at 1,000 × g for 1 min at 24 °C; discard supernatant.
Add 400 µL L‑15 medium containing 0.1 % collagenase; incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Tap gently, then centrifuge again at 1,000 × g for 1 min at 24 °C; discard supernatant.
Add 200 µL EDTA‑containing PBS(–) (0.1 mM EDTA in Dulbecco’s PBS); incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.
Tap gently, centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 1 min at 24 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in M2 medium and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Under a stereomicroscope, collect visible oocytes with a glass capillary (inner diameter slightly larger than the ~50 µm oocyte).

steps.title: Collect immature oocytes from adult mice
steps.instruction: Obtain oocytes from adult females using the same enzymatic and washing steps as for juveniles.

substeps.instruction: Follow steps D1–D11 (tissue dissection, collagenase digestion, EDTA wash, centrifugation).
After the final 10‑min M2 suspension, pick oocytes visually under a stereomicroscope with a capillary.

steps.title: Monitor calcium oscillations in oocytes
steps.instruction: Load oocytes with Oregon Green 488 BAPTA‑1 AM, perform live‑cell imaging, and quantify fluorescence changes.

substeps.instruction: Incubate ~100 immature oocytes in TYH medium containing 2 µM Oregon Green 488 BAPTA‑1 AM for 15 min at 37 °C in a 5 % CO₂ incubator.
Wash oocytes three times with fresh TYH medium, each wash lasting 5 min.
Place oocytes in a stage‑top incubator that maintains temperature, humidity, and 5 % CO₂ for live imaging.
Acquire fluorescence images with a CCD camera every 10 s using the microscope setup (Olympus UIS2 UPLANFL 10× objective, 25 µm pinhole, scanning speed up to 2,000 fps, excitation 405–640 nm).
Using Andor iQ software, subtract the baseline fluorescence (F₀) from each frame (F) to obtain F/F₀ ratios; keep all acquisition parameters constant across samples.
Define a region of interest covering most of each oocyte and measure mean intensity for each time point automatically.
Report calcium dynamics as the F/F₀ ratio over time.

Optimize exposure (50–300 ms) to avoid pixel saturation; monitor intensity histograms and adjust laser power to minimize photobleaching and phototoxicity. Acquire Z‑stacks covering the full oocyte volume at 1 µm intervals (or single optical sections) and generate maximum‑intensity projections for analysis.
